// why: TypeScript is used for types and nothing else. Node 22.18+ strips them and
runs the file, so this project has no build step and needs no install to
run — `node main.ts` is the whole story.
erasableSyntaxOnly is what keeps that true. Parameter properties, enums and
namespaces are all valid TypeScript that Node refuses to run, and neither
`node --check` nor a plain `tsc --noEmit` rejects them: the first ignores
types entirely, the second correctly says the code is legal. Without this
flag the first parameter property somebody writes breaks clone-and-run, and
it breaks it for the viewer rather than for us.
